newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty falls as some hot foreign capital exits.
newsitem.headline: Zloty falls as some hot foreign capital exits.

text.p: The zloty sank nearly half a percentage point on Thursday as some shorter-term foreign investors sold Polish paper while hopes of a continually strong zloty slowly faded in light of a mounting current account gap.

Dealers said Polish banks started to rebuild currency positions in early trade after cutting them on Wednesday and that the light currency buying trend was soon strengthened by an estimated $50 million of foreigner withdrawal on Thursday.
"Trade was nervous so even a small withdrawal created large zloty swings, but it seems that mainly short-term papers were sold," said one dealer at a large Polish bank.
The Polish zloty hit a four-week low of 1.15/1.03 percent from the trading band centre on Thursday, against Wednesday's 1.53/1.51 percent close.
It closed at 3.2570/00 to the dollar, down from 3.2372/75 on Wednesday and at 1.8830/60 to the mark, down from 1.8778/83.
Dealers said that zloty moves in the short-term future were not clear, but that in order to go lower the zloty would first have to break through support at one percent from parity.
"It is not likely that Polish banks have turned fully bearish on the zloty, even though some hot capital is leaving," said Witold Wozniak, dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.

Earlier this week the central bank said Poland's external deficit would spiral out of control in 1998 unless next year's budget was balanced. The goverment said a balanced budget was impossible in 1998, but that it would cut next year's deficit.

The Finance Minister said however that a tight monetary policy and planned cuts in the 1998 budget gap would cool domestic demand enough to keep the current account below critical levels of eight percent of GDP next year.
Poland's trade deficit was seen at about $12 billion this year, up from $8.2 billion in 1996, while the C/A gap was expected to hit $6 billion, against $1.4 billion in 1996.

"Factors such as controversy over next year's budget and a decreasing upside potential for the zloty amid a growing C/A gap probably caused Thursday's small withdrawal," said Krzysztof Kozuchowski, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

Poland's money market remained tight as banks squared positions before the monthly reserve period end on June 29, but dealers said that overnight rates may ease on Friday as there seemed to be some surplus funds on the market.
O/N rates closed at 23.0/24.10 percent, down from opening's 23.8/24.6. Tomorrow/next were at 22.80/24.05 percent, down from 23.70/24.50.
